question: The budget proposed for the future Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2028-2034 is EUR 300 billion, or 15 % less than the current budget. This raises questions in connection with food security and this as a strategic priority for the EU. Farmers and farming are the backbone of the EU, but go unseen.
They typically receive between 7-10 % of the retail price of a food product, and rely on the subsidies expected from the CAP as a source of income.

Despite this situation, the reduction in CAP funding for the 2028-2034 period will feed into lower subsidies and, although an inflation adjustment clause has been provided for, there are no indications as to how this will impact on CAP subsidies for candidate countries to the EU when they join the Union. 1.
What are the potential scenarios for European agriculture should one or more candidate countries join the EU, especially as regards direct payments under the CAP?
How does the Commission plan to protect European farmers, with a reduced budget, in the event of a future enlargement of the EU?
What is the strategy for supporting and successfully integrating farmers from future Member States into the CAP, and what funding will be allocated for this?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.11.2025) 1. Building on the Vision for Agriculture and Food, the Commission’s proposal for a future Common Agricultural Policy (CAP)1 emphasises further simplification, directing support to farmers who need it most and finding the right balance between obligations and incentives, investments and additional sources of financing.

Agriculture and rural areas also stand to gain from funding opportunities and synergies with other policy areas, with the CAP integrated into the National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPP). These elements go in the right direction to make the CAP fit for an enlarged Union. 2. The amount identified for the CAP is EUR 300 billion for 2028-2034, including at least EUR 293.

7 billion ring-fenced for income support and an allocation of EUR 6.3 billion to address market disturbances through the Unity Safety Net. Each Member State can increase its contribution to agriculture by tapping into the unallocated amounts in their overall allocation under the NRPP. The proposal for 2028-20342 includes a clause for revision when the timing of enlargement is known. 3.

To support farmers from enlargement countries and help countries prepare for the implementation of the CAP, the EU focuses on gradual alignment, technical assistance, and financial support. Key elements of this include strengthening the administrative capacity of their authorities, promoting sustainable agricultural practices, and fostering economic diversification in rural areas.

For the period post 2027, the Commission proposal establishing ‘Global Europe’3 provides a significant increase in EU funding for the Europe pillar, including enlargement countries, to accelerate their alignment with EU values, laws, rules, standards, policies and practices.
